events.title: England and Scotland Unite as Great Britain
events.description: The Acts of Union took effect, merging the kingdoms of England and Scotland into a single state, the Kingdom of Great Britain, with one parliament at Westminster.
events.significance: It created the British state that would grow into a global empire and industrial power. The union still shapes debates about national identity in the United Kingdom.

events.title: The Empire State Building Opens
events.description: President Herbert Hoover pressed a button in Washington, D.C., to switch on the lights of the 102-story Empire State Building in New York City. The building was dedicated that day.
events.significance: It was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years. It became a lasting symbol of New York and of American ambition during the Great Depression.

events.title: German Radio Announces Hitler's Death
events.description: As the Red Army closed in on Berlin, German radio told listeners that Adolf Hitler had fallen at his command post. The broadcast falsely said he died fighting. In fact he had taken his own life the day before.
events.significance: The announcement signaled the imminent collapse of Nazi Germany. Germany's surrender came days later, ending the war in Europe.

events.title: U-2 Spy Plane Shot Down Over the Soviet Union
events.description: American pilot Francis Gary Powers was flying a Lockheed U-2 reconnaissance aircraft when it was shot down over Sverdlovsk Oblast in the Soviet Union.
events.significance: The incident set off a major diplomatic crisis. It helped wreck a planned superpower summit in Paris and deepened Cold War tensions.
